question: Can broker-branch net buying/selling be interpreted as a single main-force or beneficial-owner position?
officialSemantics: TWSE buy/sell daily reports contain stock, broker/branch, execution price, buy shares and sell shares.
TWSE states broker stock trading data combine proprietary-dealer and brokerage-client transactions.
Where a broker has head office and branches, proprietary activity is aggregated into head office in the full daily report.
The complete all-stock ex-warrant branch report is a paid daily product; hot-stock/hot-broker subsets are separate selected products.
positiveMechanisms: Persistent same-branch concentration may proxy repeated order routing, coordinated demand, client clustering or dealer activity.
Cross-branch breadth/concentration may describe whether observed demand is diffuse or concentrated.
falsification: One branch can aggregate many unrelated customers.
One investor can route through multiple brokers/branches.
Head-office rows may include proprietary trading, so customer intent is not identifiable.
A branch can switch client mix across time; branch name is not a stable beneficial-owner label.
Using only hot-stock/hot-broker tables conditions on attention/turnover and can manufacture apparent predictive strength.
Net branch buying can be inventory transfer, hedging, arbitrage or liquidity provision rather than directional conviction.
exactNext: Before any alpha test, freeze broker/branch code vintage and a complete-universe source contract. Do not substitute hot-stock subsets. If no authorized full-universe source exists, keep broker-branch signals research-only/UNKNOWN rather than scrape vendor leaderboards.
